headline: Profit slips on weaker material sales, dividend raised
summary_short: Universal Display's Q2 2026 revenue was $152.2M (+7.0% q/q, -11.4% y/y) and diluted EPS fell to $1.06 (-24.8% y/y) as material sales dropped 25% y/y, though the Board raised the quarterly dividend to $0.50/share and added a $400M buyback authorization.
summary_long: Revenue fell 11.4% y/y to $152.2M (+7.0% q/q) as material sales dropped 25% y/y to $66.2M on lower unit volume and mix, while royalty and license fees rose 7% to $81.2M on a favorable catch-up adjustment. Gross margin narrowed to 76% from 77%. Operating income fell 21.7% y/y to $53.6M and net income fell 26.5% y/y to $49.4M ($1.06 diluted EPS, -24.8% y/y), as lower R&D/SG&A couldn't offset the gross-profit decline, plus an FX swing and lower investment income. Total cash and investments fell to $854.5M from $955.4M at 2025 year-end after $114.2M of buybacks and $46.6M of dividends. The Board added a $400M buyback authorization and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.50/share.

drivers.explanation: Profitability declined y/y as weaker OLED material sales volume outweighed higher royalty/license fees, while the Board expanded its buyback authorization by $400M and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.50/share.

Material sales fell 25% y/y on lower unit volume, customer mix shifts, and an unfavorable catch-up adjustment change, partially offset by royalty/license revenue up 7% on a favorable catch-up adjustment.
Gross margin narrowed to 76% from 77% as the revenue mix shifted toward lower-margin material sales relative to royalty and license fee revenue.
Lower gross profit outweighed a modest reduction in R&D and SG&A expenses for the quarter, per the release's own line-item discussion.
Lower operating income combined with a swing to a foreign-exchange loss (vs. a prior-year FX gain on the Korean Won receivable) and lower interest/investment income.
EPS fell less steeply than net income y/y (-24.8% vs -26.5%) because diluted share count fell 2.1% y/y from ongoing buybacks.
Cost of sales decreased on lower material sales volume and lower Adesis contract-research costs, partially offset by unfavorable product mix.
Total liquidity (cash + short-term + long-term investments) fell to $854.5M from $955.4M at 2025 year-end after $168.6M used in financing, including $114.2M of buybacks and $46.6M of dividends paid.
Share count fell as the Board's $100M repurchase program (completed in H1 2026) and a new $400M authorization (April 2026) funded $114.2M of H1 2026 buybacks.
